title: Connected Data London 2024 Educational Track Review and Unconference | Panel
description:
How do you model something as human and elusive as a “vibe”? And what can urban serendipity teach us about ontologies, knowledge graphs, AI, and the future of data?

In this lively discussion, experts in ontology, graph technology, data modeling, visualization, and enterprise AI explore how we can turn complex, human concepts into structured, computable knowledge.

The conversation begins with urban serendipity and quickly evolves into a fascinating live exploration of how to build a draft ontology of vibe. What exactly is a vibe? Is it an emotion, a property of a space, an emergent phenomenon, or something created through interactions between people, movement, sound, symbols, and context?

From there, the discussion connects seemingly abstract ontology questions to very practical challenges in enterprise data and AI. The speakers examine why organizations need to organize their data before they can become truly AI-ready, how ontologies can align large language models with organizational knowledge, and why the purpose of a knowledge graph matters more than simply putting data into a graph database.

The session also explores:

• Urban serendipity and the future of cities
• How to create an ontology of vibe
• Knowledge graphs, graph engines, and graph databases
• Enterprise data modeling and AI readiness
• BFO (Basic Formal Ontology) and ontology layers
• Modeling emergent phenomena, thresholds, time, and causality
• Data-driven ontology design and working with subject-matter experts
• Competency questions and how to design ontologies around real use cases
• Graph visualization and the risk of introducing bias through visual choices
• Symbolic AI, vector databases, LLMs, and hybrid AI systems
• Why AI systems need to know what they know—and what they don't know
• How ontology, graphs, and structured data can support better decision-making

One of the most memorable parts of the session is a live “data therapy” exercise, where the group collaboratively tries to identify the concepts, relationships, observations, and signals that could make up a computable model of vibe.

The result is an engaging discussion about where knowledge representation, ontologies, knowledge graphs, AI, human behavior, and complex systems meet—and how asking better questions can lead to better models and better answers.

🎯 Topics: Ontology, Knowledge Graphs, Graph Databases, AI, Generative AI, LLMs, Symbolic AI, Data Modeling, Knowledge Representation, Enterprise AI, Graph Visualization, BFO, Complex Systems, Urban Serendipity
